translation.english_title: O girl born to a blind father!

source_tamil_lines: எண்ணற்ற பொய் சொல்லி என்னையே மாற்றிய என் தங்கமே!
வானை நோக்கித் திரையைப் போட்டால் வட்ட நிலவும்
கெட்டிக்காரன் பொய்யும் புரட்டும் எட்டு நாளைக்கு - இந்தக்
கட்டிக் கரும்பின் பொய்யும் புரட்டும் எத்தனை நாளைக்கு? ஆ!
english_lines: O girl born to a blind father!
My gold, who told countless lies and changed even me!
If a cat closes its eyes, will the whole world turn dark,
If a curtain is drawn facing the sky, will the round moon,
A clever man's lies and twists last eight days — but this,
Bundled sugarcane's lies and twists — how many days will they last? Ah!
notes: The opening `வீணா / வாலி / போலி` sound-chain is retained through transliteration rather than replaced with an invented English rhyme.
The cat/world and curtain/moon ridicule remains concrete and theatrical.
`கட்டிக் கரும்பு` is retained conservatively as `bundled sugarcane`; the line carries comic metaphor/wordplay that should not be over-resolved.

english_lines: I didn't tell any lies at all,
notes: The source itself switches from song to dialogue; that division remains explicit.

english_lines: O girl from the house next door to Harishchandra!
In speaking truth so unjustly, who,
On this earth can equal you, dear!
notes: The Harishchandra reference and the sarcasm of `அநியாயமாய் உண்மை` are kept together rather than normalized into a plain accusation of lying.
The nested source speaker labels remain visible inside the dialogue section.

source_tamil_lines: கிளாவர் ராணி! உனக்கு என்ன வேணுமின்னு கேளு!...
english_lines: Like the queen in a deck of cards,
Clavar Queen! Ask what you want!...
Dance like the queen of dance,
What anger have you against me?
Is it the sin of telling the truth?
What yearning is in your heart?
notes: The source card-suit forms `கிளாவர்`, `டைமன்`, and `இஸ்பேட்` are retained as `Clavar`, `Daiman`, and `Ispade` instead of silently regularizing them to modern English suit names.
`சீட்டுக் கட்டு ராணி` remains explicitly the queen in a deck of cards, preserving the running queen/card joke.
Animal/bird vocatives such as peahen and flower-cuckoo remain concrete.

translator_notes: This two-page record intentionally preserves the anthology's interleaving of spoken dialogue and song; neither layer is discarded.
The comic sarcasm, proverbial logic, card-game vocabulary and colloquial register are retained rather than rewritten into polished romantic banter.
PDF 58–59 provenance remains attached to one translation record.
